sidebars.body_markdown: A company can fund a buyback only from free reserves, the securities premium account, or the proceeds of a fresh issue of shares. It cannot use the proceeds of an earlier issue of the same kind of shares. This prevents the company from effectively returning capital it just raised. The restriction ensures that buybacks are funded from genuine surplus, not recycled IPO or rights issue money.
sidebars.rationale: Sidebar consolidates the three allowed sources and the restriction, which are listed in the prose but benefit from a compact reference.
